body_md: We comment on our motivation for recording $L^{\infty}(Q)$ estimates. We observe from \eqref{H_m_estimates_1} and \eqref{H_m_estimates_0} that an $\mathcal{O}(\rho^{-1})$ estimate for the remainder $r(x,t)$ requires $N \geq 2m + 1$. On the other hand, such a remainder estimate can be fulfilled by taking $N = 3$ in \eqref{L_infty_estimates_1} and \eqref{L_infty_estimates_0}. This smaller choice of $N$ allows us to reduce the regularity required for $p_{j}$ in the forthcoming arguments.

title: Remark
body_md: We can define the solution for $t \in (-T, 0)$ by taking $v^{(l)}_{j}(x,t) = \overline{v^{(l)}_{j}(x,-t)}$ (this is why we assumed $f^{(j)}_{l}$ was real-valued in Theorem \ref{main_theorem_other_setting}) and $r_{j}(x,t) = -\overline{r_{j}(x,-t)}$. This allows one to use the Carleman estimate from Proposition \ref{standard_Schrodinger_Carleman_estimate_0} and to bound $\Vert \partial r/\partial \nu\Vert_{L^{2}(\Gamma_{j} \times (-T, T))}$ by a constant times $\Vert \partial r/\partial \nu\Vert_{L^{2}(\Sigma_{j})}$.
